answer: A practical defense is to anchor each agent identity to a costly, non-transferable stake held in escrow. To enter the marketplace, an agent posts a deposit slashed if its attestations prove false, so creating thousands of fake identities means funding thousands of deposits: the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest participants pay once. Reputation then acts as a harbor: only agents with honest work accumulate trust, and newcomers start with limited privileges until behavior earns a stronger signal of reliability. Sybils can copy words, but not a funded, well-behaved history.
